name: SendGrid
verdict: No OAuth app was found. Each customer's owner or admin creates a restricted API key and pastes it in, about 1-3 days; reseller or provisioning routes need a formal Twilio SendGrid partnership.
needGuide: No — just collect a restricted API key from each customer (Settings → API Keys).

auth.detail: v3 APIs use an API key as Authorization: Bearer <key>; SMTP uses username 'apikey' with the key as password. No customer-facing OAuth was found in the docs read. Parent accounts can act for Subusers with the On-Behalf-Of header; customer accounts exist only for formal Twilio SendGrid resellers.

effort.timeToProduction: 1-3 days (no review) on the API-key path; reseller partnership timeline unknown

approval.gate: None for the API-key path. A customer account-provisioning or reseller route (Account Provisioning API, 'customer accounts' under On-Behalf-Of) requires a formal reseller partnership with Twilio SendGrid, which was not documented in detail here. Sending mail also requires sender authentication in practice (not confirmed in the pages read).

scopes.why: No OAuth; ask customers for a restricted key with mail.send and only the other permissions you use.
scopes.summary: Key permission levels: Full Access, Custom/Restricted Access (pick endpoints and read/write levels), Billing Access, and Email Address Validation Access. Billing-related calls need a separate key. Ask customers for a restricted key with mail.send and only the other scopes you use.

cost: Free to integrate; the customer needs their own SendGrid plan
prerequisites: Account and owner: A developer with a SendGrid account for a test key; for the partner route, a business contact negotiating a reseller agreement with Twilio SendGrid.
Where you register: Customer's SendGrid console -> Settings -> API Keys -> Create API Key -> choose permissions -> Create & View
Cost: Free to integrate; the customer needs their own SendGrid plan

registerAt.path: Customer's SendGrid console -> Settings -> API Keys -> Create API Key -> choose permissions -> Create & View

steps.do: Customer opens Settings -> API Keys -> Create API Key, names it for your app, picks Restricted/Custom Access with only the needed scopes
Customer clicks Create & View and copies the key (shown only once) into your connect screen
Store the key encrypted per customer; never log it or commit it
Validate with GET https://api.sendgrid.com/v3/scopes using Bearer auth and compare returned scopes to what you need
Use api.eu.sendgrid.com for EU regional subusers; use the On-Behalf-Of header only if you are the parent account (it does not work with Mail Send)
If you need one-click onboarding, contact Twilio SendGrid about partner or reseller provisioning

roles.team: A developer with a SendGrid account for a test key; for the partner route, a business contact negotiating a reseller agreement with Twilio SendGrid.
roles.console: Teammates are managed in the SendGrid console; a key cannot have greater permissions than its creator, so use an admin to create keys.
roles.customer: The account owner or an admin teammate creates the key and pastes it into your app. Subuser access requires the Pro or Premier plan.

testing: Use your own SendGrid account and a restricted test key; limits apply per plan.
Accounts are limited to 100 API keys.

blockers.problem: A key cannot exceed its creator's permissions
blockers.fix: A non-admin teammate may be unable to grant what you need.

blockers.problem: The key is shown only once
blockers.fix: A lost key requires creating a new one.

blockers.problem: On-Behalf-Of does not support Mail Send and needs the parent account's key
blockers.fix: It is not a way to access an unrelated customer's account.

blockers.problem: No OAuth means no consent screen or scoped revocation outside the key itself

automation.agentCan: Write the key storage and validation code, draft customer setup instructions with the exact scopes, run test calls and sample sends.
automation.humanMust: Customer creates and pastes the key; a human negotiates any reseller or partner agreement and handles legal acceptance.

uncertain: The Account Provisioning API page failed to fetch and no OAuth or technology-partner program was found; the 2FA requirement, current free-plan status and sender-authentication rules were not confirmed.
Search and fetch budgets ran out before community sources were checked.
